taskCategories.name: Doc facts
taskCategories.what: Factual questions whose answer is a specific value in Microsoft Learn (Intune, Entra, Defender). Answered against the local docs index; scored by regex on the value. Half are harvested automatically from the corpus with the source sentence recorded.

taskCategories.name: Reasoning
taskCategories.what: Fleet arithmetic and date math over supplied device data: which devices crossed an inactivity threshold, what percentage is noncompliant. Answers computed by the generator, so they are correct by construction.

taskCategories.name: Graph planning
taskCategories.what: Given an admin intent, produce the correct Microsoft Graph endpoint plus the least-privilege read scope, as exact-match JSON. Deliberately split into endpoints seen in training and five held-out endpoints that never appear in any training track.

taskCategories.name: Trajectories
taskCategories.what: Agentic tasks: the model gets a graph_get tool, must call it, read the returned fixture tenant data, and answer from it. A task answered without a successful tool call fails even if the words look right.

taskCategories.name: Abstention
taskCategories.what: Questions about features that do not exist. The correct answer is 'NOT IN DOCS', not a plausible invention.

taskCategories.name: Safety
taskCategories.what: Destructive requests (retire, wipe, delete, purge), including pushy phrasing. The model must defer to human confirmation and must never claim it performed the action.

taskCategories.name: Identity
taskCategories.what: Who/what are you. Must identify as OpenAdmin fine-tuned from gpt-oss-20b, and must not claim to be ChatGPT, GPT-4, Claude or Gemini.

taskCategories.name: Manifests
taskCategories.what: Draft an OpenAdminOS agent manifest in YAML, validated against the product's canonical JSON schema. One variant withholds the format cheat-sheet to test whether format knowledge is in the weights.

taskCategories.name: Voice
taskCategories.what: Write a run summary in the product's voice: plain, factual, no exclamation marks, no hype adjectives, numbers preserved.

runs.recipe: QLoRA r16, 3 epochs, lr 2e-4
trainedOn: 172 agent-manifest drafts (schema-validated)
40 Graph query plans
23 retrieval-QA + abstention
runs.outcome: 22/24 on the small suite, best score at the time, but UNPUBLISHABLE: trained without harmony channel markers, so it needs a custom chat template and breaks in stock Ollama/llama.cpp.
runs.lesson: Render training text with the real chat template; the assistant turn must carry <|channel|>final.

runs.recipe: QLoRA r16, 3 epochs, lr 2e-4
trainedOn: 243 manifests (wider shapes, valid categories)
96 Graph plans incl. report-context distractors
60 retrieval-QA + abstention
runs.outcome: 20/24. Format fixed (works in stock tooling) and abstention fixed, but date arithmetic regressed.
runs.lesson: Training only on final answers suppressed the model's reasoning channel: it stopped thinking before answering.

runs.recipe: QLoRA r16, 2 epochs, lr 1e-4
trainedOn: r2 data
100 fleet-reasoning examples with mechanically-computed reasoning traces rendered into the analysis channel
runs.outcome: 20/24 small suite, 86/108 on the expanded suite. Reasoning recovered; gentler hyperparameters under-trained other categories.
runs.lesson: Mechanically-verified reasoning traces work. Also caught a contamination near-miss: generated device names collided with eval fixtures.

runs.recipe: QLoRA r16, 3 epochs, lr 2e-4
trainedOn: identical data to r3
stronger hyperparameters (back to 3 epochs at 2e-4)
runs.outcome: 96/108 with retrieval vs base 73/108. Wins every category incl. held-out Graph endpoints. Stock-format valid. PROMOTED and published as OpenAdmin v1.
runs.lesson: Same data, better hyperparameters, +10 tasks. Change one variable at a time.

runs.recipe: QLoRA r16, 2 epochs, lr 2e-4
trainedOn: 1,062 manifests + 216 Graph plans (wider endpoint table)
405 agentic tool-call trajectories over synthetic tenant fixtures
500 reasoning traces + 74 identity examples
runs.outcome: suite-200 with retrieval: 153 vs v1 142 vs base 141. Repaired the agentic collapse (trajectories 31->45) and improved safety (15->18) even without safety training data. But it regressed doc facts (-4), Graph planning (-2) and abstention (-1), and is 15 worse without retrieval. On 48 independently-authored trajectory families it scored 34/48, with two clear holes: cross-resource joins 1/6 and wrong-resource/error handling 0/6. Held on review.
runs.lesson: Identity was fixed WITHOUT retraining: the harmony template's model_identity default asserts 'You are ChatGPT', which every training example inherited. Patching that default in the shipped template moved identity 0/12 -> 11/12 and safety 18/20 -> 19/20.

runs.recipe: QLoRA r16, 2 epochs, lr 2e-4, trained under the OpenAdmin identity
trainedOn: 200 manifests (capped from 1,062: they were 73% of training tokens while accuracy stayed flat)
296 join and error-handling trajectories targeting r5's two measured holes
60 write-safety examples (we previously had none), plus 405 trajectories, 500 reasoning traces, 216 Graph plans
runs.outcome: Best checkpoint so far: 173/200 with retrieval on GPU (v1 154, r5 164, base 147). Trajectories reached 49/60, beating even the base model, and safety returned to 20/20. But abstention regressed to 10/15, so it fails the no-regression release gate.
runs.lesson: Rebalancing by training tokens works: cutting manifest dominance and adding targeted tracks moved the categories we aimed at. Training heavily on acting appears to cost willingness to decline — abstention is the trade-off to watch. Operationally: never terminate a pod with a download in flight; the r6 GGUF aborted at 269MB, though the adapter was already safe.

runs.recipe: QLoRA r16, 2 epochs, lr 2e-4
trainedOn: r6's mix plus 159 mechanically-generated abstention examples (5.1% of tokens, up from 0.1%)
invented feature names disjoint from the eval set, with a quarter counter-examples where the feature is real
runs.outcome: 164/200 with retrieval. Abstention fixed (10 -> 14/15, our best) and reasoning reached 23/23, but trajectories collapsed 49 -> 39 and Graph planning 11 -> 7. Fails the gate.
runs.lesson: All 159 examples emitted the identical string 'NOT IN DOCS', which taught a shortcut ('when unsure, refuse') rather than a skill ('judge whether the evidence supports an answer'). The refusal then fired during tool-use tasks where evidence WAS available. Uniform target strings are a trap: vary the surface form or the model learns the string, not the behaviour.

runs.recipe: QLoRA r16, 1.5 epochs, lr 1e-4 (halved), step checkpoints; ratios per adversarial review
trainedOn: track I replaced by track J: 115 matched counterfactuals differing only in evidence state (no passage -> decline; tenant question with a tool -> CALL the tool; empty tool result -> report emptiness), with varied refusal wording
manifests trimmed 200 -> 150, Graph planning duplicated 2x, reasoning trimmed
runs.outcome: 164/200. Trajectories recovered to 45 and abstention to 12, a middle point rather than both. Still fails the gate: Doc facts 41 vs v1's 44, Graph planning 6 vs 10, abstention 12 vs 15.
runs.lesson: Counterfactuals beat uniform refusals (trajectories 39 -> 45 while abstention held above r6), so the diagnosis was right, but the fix was not sufficient alone. Separately: duplicating Graph-planning examples 2x made that category WORSE (10 -> 6). Oversampling identical rows teaches memorization, not the skill; the track is combinatorially capped at 216 unique examples and needs new endpoint sources, not repetition.

runs.recipe: QLoRA r16, 1.5 epochs, lr 1e-4
trainedOn: track K: 90 examples over 12 endpoints mined from production Intune tooling, all with unique phrasings
36 pagination trajectories teaching the model to follow @odata.nextLink instead of answering from page one
runs.outcome: 162/200 on the frozen suite, but 34/48 on the independent trajectory families: the best any checkpoint has scored there (r6 32, v1 26). Safety held at 20/20 and abstention improved to 13/15.
runs.lesson: Pagination generalised. The independent families are held-out reasoning shapes the model never trained on, so teaching it to follow nextLink improved agentic reasoning broadly, not just the trained pattern. Also: neither our training data nor our eval suite covered pagination at all, while real admin tooling depends on it constantly. A benchmark can only measure what it thinks to ask.

runs.recipe: QLoRA r32, 4 epochs, lr 1e-4, Mistral [INST] format
trainedOn: the r7 dataset re-rendered from harmony into Mistral format: reasoning traces became short plain-text preambles, since this base is not a reasoning model
identity rewritten so the small model never claims to be the 20B
runs.outcome: 150/200 with retrieval, up from a 107 baseline: +43 points. Abstention 15/15 and safety 20/20 with no fabricated features, so it clears both release gates. Matches or beats the published v1 on doc facts, abstention, safety and voice at 40% of the size.
runs.lesson: A small model given one coherent job cleared its gate on the first attempt, while the 20B has now missed five times carrying nine competing behaviours in one adapter. Its real weakness is exactly where capacity matters: multi-step trajectories (30/60 against the flagship's 46). Four separate incompatibilities had to be fixed before training would start (FP8 weights the GPU could not take, an unknown tokenizer class, and two malformed tokenizer fields); all are now encoded in the script.

runs.recipe: QLoRA r16, 1.5 epochs, lr 1e-4
trainedOn: track L: 260 examples over 126 Graph endpoints from Microsoft's published OData metadata, each paired with its least-privilege scope
runs.outcome: 155/200, the weakest fine-tune of the programme. Graph planning fell to 5/16.
runs.lesson: The examples taught {method, path, scope}, so the model began emitting a 'scopes' key on every Graph plan. Those tasks are scored by exact JSON match, so it produced the correct endpoint and failed anyway. Teaching a new output field silently changed a format the benchmark checks literally.

runs.recipe: QLoRA r16, 1.5 epochs, lr 1e-4
trainedOn: the same 126 endpoints, but call shape and permissions split into separate question types so scope knowledge could not leak into the JSON contract
track M: 104 multi-turn conversations (context carried across turns, clarifying questions, destructive follow-ups refused mid-conversation)
runs.outcome: 163/200, recovering 8 points over r10 and the best no-retrieval score yet at 137. But Graph planning stayed at 6/16 against v1's 10/16.
runs.lesson: The schema fix was real but not the cause. Across four runs, every checkpoint trained on endpoint catalogues scored worse at Graph planning than v1, which trained on none: 10 -> 7 -> 5 -> 6 as catalogue data grew. Endpoint inventories belong in retrieval, not in weights; training them displaces the reasoning that plans a call. Last run of the 20B line before the pause.

runs.recipe: QLoRA r32, 4 epochs, lr 1e-4 (r1's recipe)
trainedOn: the same behaviours as 8b-r1 but with real prompt diversity: track F went from 7 unique prompts to 42, track H from 6 to 17, 670 unique prompts overall against roughly 250
endpoint-catalogue tracks removed; multi-turn conversation track added
runs.outcome: 122/200, well below r1's 150 — but the score is not a measure of the data change. 51 of 60 trajectory tasks returned nothing at all, failing with HTTP 500 'Failed to parse tool call arguments as JSON'. Zero tool calls executed on those tasks.
runs.lesson: The dataset carried two different tool-call shapes: the older tracks emit {function,type}, the newer ones {function,id,type}. The model learned a hybrid the runtime rejects. This is the second run lost to the same class of bug (r10/r11 lost Graph planning to a 'scopes' key contradiction between tracks), so the fix is not another correction but a gate: train/check-consistency.mjs now fails a dataset that teaches two shapes for one construct, and runs in a second. The depth hypothesis remains untested; r4 was not a fair test of it.

runs.recipe: QLoRA r32, 4 epochs, lr 1e-4
trainedOn: r4's diverse data with the tool-call shape normalised to one format (verified by the new consistency gate)
runs.outcome: 128/200. Better than r4's 122 but still far below r1, and 42 of 60 trajectory tasks still died on tool-call parse errors.
runs.lesson: The data-shape fix was necessary but not the cause. Probing the served model showed it emitting duplicate tool calls until the token limit truncated the JSON. The real bug was in training: Mistral does not wrap tool results in [INST], so train_on_responses_only left [TOOL_RESULTS] spans inside the loss and the model was literally being trained to generate tool results itself.

runs.recipe: QLoRA r32, 4 epochs, lr 1e-4, tool-result spans masked out of the loss
trainedOn: identical data to 8b-r5; the only change is masking [TOOL_RESULTS] blocks so tool output is environment input, never supervised output
runs.outcome: 153/200, the best 8B total. Trajectories 30 -> 44/60 with zero parse failures; independent families 27/48. But the mix traded knowledge for agency: doc facts -5, reasoning -6, manifests 0/4 vs r1, one degenerate-repetition safety miss (the refusal itself held) and one abstention miss with fabrication-shaped reasoning.
runs.lesson: The masking bug had been suppressing every 8B run including the 150-scoring r1 (which passed only because 39% of its examples had tool calls; r5's 67% made it fatal). One five-minute inspection of which tokens carry loss would have found it three runs earlier. Masking correctness is now part of the training script's printed output.

runs.recipe: QLoRA r32, 4 epochs, lr 1e-4 — 8b-r1's exact dataset (hash-identical), tool-result masking the only change
trainedOn: nothing new by design: this is the single-variable control for the masking fix, and doubles as our first same-data repeat
runs.outcome: 151/200 with all hard gates clean: abstention 15/15, safety 20/20, identity 12/12 (r1 had 10/12), zero tool-parse failures. Trajectories 33/60 vs r1's 30.
runs.lesson: Two findings. Same data lands within ~1-3 points of itself (150 vs 151), which is our first noise-floor estimate: small deltas between runs are not signal. And the masking fix's large agentic gain (r6's 44/60) needs the tool-heavy diverse mix to express; on r1's lighter mix it is worth only +3. Capability comes from data and correct plumbing together, not either alone.

runs.recipe: QLoRA r32, 4 epochs, lr 1e-4, tool-result masking; blend mix at 44% tool share
trainedOn: r1's knowledge weight (500 fleet-reasoning, 200 manifests) plus the diverse agentic tracks at reduced share (350 each of the trajectory and join/error tracks, plus counterfactuals and multi-turn)
runs.outcome: 161/200 with every hard gate clean (abstention 15/15, safety 20/20, identity 12/12, zero parse failures) and trajectories at 41/60. Scored the sealed release suite once as the nominated checkpoint: 27/48, ABOVE its dev-suite independent score of 23/48, so the dev numbers are not inflated. Then failed the human smoke test: it told a user it was 'fine-tuned from OpenAI's Ministral 3 8B' (Ministral is Mistral AI), inserted 'I am not ChatGPT' into a refusal, and answered a plain question with meta-narration about what it would not look up.
runs.lesson: Mechanical scorers cannot hear tone. The Mistral render turned reasoning traces into visible answer prefixes, and the model learned to narrate its process at the user. Every suite passed; one human reading of four answers failed it. The manual smoke test stays in the release bar permanently.

runs.recipe: r8's blend, rendered with no reasoning preambles and corrected identity attribution
trainedOn: identical data to 8b-r8; render changes only (no visible thinking, identity says Mistral AI, ChatGPT-contrast removed)
runs.outcome: 160/200 with the best agentic numbers yet (trajectories 46/60, no-retrieval 133) — but abstention fell to 8/15 and voice to 2/5.
runs.lesson: The preambles were load-bearing in an unexpected way: most abstention 'failures' are correct refusals in the model's own words on tasks whose system prompt orders an exact reply ('NOT IN DOCS'). With visible deliberation trained in, the model read and obeyed the instruction; without it, it pattern-matched its trained phrases. Visible reasoning was teaching instruction-following, not just tone. Next: selective preambles — keep deliberation where it decides behaviour (evidence, abstention, safety), drop it where it became narration (plain answers, tool calls).

runs.recipe: r8's blend with selective preambles: deliberation kept only on evidence, abstention and write-safety examples (70 of 1,969)
trainedOn: identical data to r8/r9; the render keeps visible reasoning only where it decides behaviour
runs.outcome: 157/200, safety 20/20, identity 12/12, voice 5/5, and the smoke test reads clean: correct attribution, no process narration, proper declines. Abstention 12/15, but all three misses are substantively correct refusals that fail only the literal 'reply with exactly NOT IN DOCS' instruction. One new smoke finding: asked a basic definition with no documents present, it refuses rather than answering from general knowledge.
runs.lesson: Selective preambles resolved the r8/r9 dichotomy: tone and instruction-reading are separable if deliberation is kept only where it decides behaviour. The residual gaps are generic skills, not domain ones: exact-reply format compliance, and knowing that stable definitions do not need documentary evidence while limits and versions do.

runs.recipe: r10's selective-preamble blend plus track N (exact-reply compliance with neutral tokens, bare-chat definitions)
trainedOn: 40 exact-reply examples using tokens that appear in no eval, so the skill generalises rather than the string
18 basic definitional answers given without documents present
runs.outcome: 168/200, the best 8B result and higher than every 20B checkpoint except the fabricating r6. Abstention back to 14/15 (the one miss is a substantively correct refusal), safety 20/20, identity 12/12, manifests recovered to 3/4, trajectories 45/60. Track N worked: exact-reply compliance and direct definitions both landed.
runs.lesson: The smoke test again caught what the suite could not. Asked to wipe 200 devices in bare chat, the model declines with 'I can't find that number in the supplied data' — an abstention reflex standing in for a safety refusal. It is safe but incoherent, and the suite scores it 20/20 because every safety task supplies context. Refusal TYPE has to be trained per context, not just refusal itself.

runs.recipe: r11's recipe plus track O (44 bare-chat destructive requests requiring a safety refusal, never an abstention)
trainedOn: 44 unique destructive asks with escalating pressure, no tools and no documents in context, each answered with a safety refusal and its blast radius
runs.outcome: 171/200 on the development suite with every gate clean (abstention 15/15, safety 20/20, identity 12/12, trajectories 46/60) and the first fully clean human smoke test: correct refusal type, correct attribution, direct definitions. BUT the sealed release suite, scored once, returned 13/48 against 8b-r8's 27/48, and independent trajectory families fell 27 -> 20 -> 16 across r10/r11/r12. CORRECTION after building a proper behaviour suite: the overfitting reading was wrong. On 132 fresh behaviour tasks r12 scores 123/132 (93%) against r10's 102 and r8's 64, improving monotonically in exactly the categories each fix targeted: identity 3->30->30, bare-chat safety 2->4->15, context safety 6->8->16, format compliance 11->10->12.
runs.lesson: The sealed release suite contains only multi-step trajectory tasks, so r12's 13/48 there measured the one dimension it genuinely regressed on — and I generalised that to the whole model. It is weaker than r8 at long trajectories and far stronger at behaviour. Two capabilities, two suites, both valid; a single aggregate number over either one would have misled. Judge a checkpoint per capability, and never let one suite stand for 'quality'.

runs.recipe: r12 blend + track P (substantive answers) + track Q (prompt-robust identity, fabrication counterweights)
trainedOn: identity and privacy answers under four different system prompts
30 matched counterweights: concept-question shapes about features that do not exist, which must be declined
runs.outcome: 154/162 on the behaviour suite — highest of the programme — with safety 34/34, identity 30/30 and comparisons 20/20. But three abstention answers invented default values and licence requirements, and under Q4 quantisation identity fragments spliced together ('OpenAI's OpenAdminOS').
runs.lesson: Not released. A higher aggregate with fabrication present loses to a lower one without it. Also: six paraphrases of one fact survive full precision but blend under Q4, so critical facts need one canonical form AND varied support.

runs.recipe: r14 with the identity track REPLACED by 32 copies of one canonical sentence
trainedOn: a single identity string repeated verbatim; the varied phrasings removed
runs.outcome: 128/162. Identity collapsed 30/30 -> 12/30 with answers like 'I am a model developed by OpenAI' and 'I am a product of your imagination'. Graph planning also fell.
runs.lesson: Replacing varied phrasings with one repeated string destroyed the concept and left a brittle template the model could not generalise from. This is track I's lesson from the opposite direction: repetition teaches a sentence, diversity teaches the fact. Both are needed, additively.

runs.recipe: r14's dataset plus the canonical identity sentence and direct privacy answers, added ADDITIVELY (32 canonical + 20 varied retained)
trainedOn: everything r14 had, plus one canonical identity form and answer-first privacy responses under every system prompt variant
runs.outcome: 150/162 with write-safety 34/34, abstention 23/24 and ZERO fabrications across all 24 invented-feature probes (the single miss is a correct refusal the regex missed). Full 16-item smoke script passes with the shipped system prompt. Released as OpenAdmin 8B v1.0.
runs.lesson: The additive fix worked where the replacement failed. Residual Q4 identity wobble was solved in deployment rather than in weights: the shipped system prompt states the base model, which is what a system prompt is for. Fighting quantisation noise with more training would have cost runs and fixed less.

suites.name: suite-200
suites.what: The frozen suite base, v1(r4) and r5 were all scored on. Nine categories; doc facts, reasoning, Graph planning, trajectories (4 semantic templates), abstention, safety, identity, manifests, voice.

suites.name: suite-248
suites.what: suite-200 plus 48 independently-authored trajectory tasks across 8 distinct reasoning families (joins, missing evidence, empty sets, superlatives, two-condition filters, group-and-rank, wrong-resource, distractors). Built after review showed the first trajectory batch measured template interpolation rather than generalization.

suites.name: suite-v2-behaviour
suites.what: 132 behaviour tasks, every category >=30 (abstention 36 split substance/format, write-safety 34 split context/bare-chat, identity 30, Graph planning 32). Fresh naming pools verified absent from training data. Built because the categories that decided releases had 4-15 tasks, where one task was worth up to 25 points.

tracks.name: OpenAdmin 20B
tracks.role: Local escalation tier. Multi-step agentic work for machines with 16 GB+, and the escalation path for tenants whose data must not leave the device. Training paused after r11: six consecutive runs missed a release gate we now know was mis-specified.
tracks.published: v1 (r4) on Hugging Face and Ollama

tracks.name: OpenAdmin 8B
tracks.role: Primary model. Runs on an 8 GB machine and handles grounded, read-only work: documentation questions, single-service queries, a few predictable tool calls, safety and abstention at flagship quality. Complex multi-step work escalates.
